data.title: EU Inks Deals With Indonesia to Cut Tariffs, Catalyze Investment
data.description:
By Ying Xian Wong and Fabiana Negrin Ochoa

The European Union signed ambitious agreements with Indonesia that eliminate most tariffs on goods between the two sides, aiming to will deliver billions in economic benefits.

Brussels announced the Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement with Indonesia on Saturday, more than 10 years after negotiations began. The parties also inked an Investment Protection Agreement to encourage bilateral flows.

"EU-Indonesia trade and investment has vast untapped potential," said Ursula von der Leyen, president of the European Commission.

Duties on main EU export products, including meat and dairy, will be removed, while existing tariffs on cars, machinery, chemicals and pharmaceuticals will be cut.

According to Indonesia's Coordinating Ministry for Economic Affairs, about 90% of tariffs on EU-bound exports to the EU will be removed, while others will be gradually reduced over 3 to 15 years or benefit from tariff-rate quotas.

The preferential access is expected to make Indonesian exports--particularly footwear, textiles and processed commodities--more competitive in the European market, it added.

The pacts open "new doors for businesses," bolstering cooperation in sectors like agri-food and advanced manufacturing, said EU Commissioner for Trade and Economic Security Maroš Šefčovič.

With the deals in place, EU shipments to Indonesia are projected to increase by nearly 40% over 15 years, while Indonesian exports of goods and services to the bloc are expected to rise by more than 14%.

"This will boost economic growth," the commission said, projecting that the EU's gross domestic product will be 16 billion euros higher and Indonesia's 27 billion euros higher, or $17.55 billion and $29.62 billion respectively.

Lowered trade barriers and streamlined investment frameworks will unlock opportunities for European businesses and farmers in Indonesia's market of 280 million consumers, the commission said. EU exporters stand to save over $650 million in annual duties.

Another key benefit for the EU is access to Indonesia's vast resources of materials like nickel and cobalt that are used in everything from electric vehicles to jet engines.

The agreement will give manufacturers stable, predictable access to critical resources, strengthening the trading bloc's supply chain against shocks, the commission said.

"It also provides an export duty-free quota for crude palm and palm kernel oil, both of which are strategic inputs for EU industries," it added.

Recent supply-chain disruptions stemming from wars and other shocks have underlined the need for countries to build up resilience via trade alliances and diversification.

The EU has already concluded agreements with Singapore and Vietnam, and is in ongoing trade negotiations with Thailand and the Philippines.

The investment and economic partnerships struck with Indonesia require the European Parliament's consent and Indonesia's internal ratification. They are expected to be provisionally applied in early 2027.

Write to Ying Xian Wong at yingxian.wong@wsj.com and Fabiana Negrin Ochoa at fabiana.negrinochoa@wsj.com

data.title: Currency Check | Rupee opens 21 paise higher at 92.46 per dollar; Asian peers trade mixed
data.description:
The Indian rupee opened higher on November 23, as a deepening technology rout has strengthened expectations of sustained foreign buying in local equities.

The rupee opened with a gain of 21 paise at 92.46 per dollar, compared with previous close of 92.67.

According to Finrex, the Indian Rupee is set to open higher at 93.54 this morning as we would be seeing FPIs inflows worth approximately USD 1 billion on Friday getting sold off today. With most markets in a down mode, India has been in the driver’s seat in respect of equities and accordingly the rupee has been gaining with a 1.6% gain last week.

The dollar index was constant at 103.76 while Brent oil was at $ 91.05 for the January contract, giving Indian equities and rupee the upside momentum.

RBI has not been buying dollars while all of oil demand is getting absorbed from the FPI inflows and balance is getting sold off in the market keeping rupee appreciated. Exporters to sell the intraday upside they get in the pair while importers can buy the dips, it added.

Asian currencies traded mixed against the US dollar, with the Chinese yuan emerging as the strongest performer, rising 0.31 percent, followed by the Taiwan dollar, which gained 0.13 percent, and the South Korean won, which edged up 0.08 percent. The Malaysian ringgit and Singapore dollar also posted marginal gains of 0.03 percent and 0.02 percent, respectively.

On the other hand, the Japanese yen was the worst performer, declining 0.19 percent, followed by the Philippine peso, which fell 0.16 percent, and the Indonesian rupiah, which slipped 0.09 percent. The Thai baht also edged lower by 0.04 percent.

The dollar eased off its highest level in more than a year and a half at the start of Asian trade on Monday, as investor confidence recovered after a selloff last week and traders pared bets that the Federal Reserve could hike interest rates aggressively at its meeting next month.

The US dollar index, which measures the greenback's strength against a basket of six currencies, was flat at 103.80, retreating from its highest levels since April 2025.

data.title: Trump renews call for Nvidia to rehire Jensen Huang as CEO
data.description:
US President Donald Trump has again urged Nvidia’s board to rehire co-founder Jensen Huang, days after the chipmaker said it did not intend to reinstate him.

“I hope the Board of Nvidia rehires Jensen Huang. It would be the best thing for the Company, and also, for the U.S.A.,” Trump wrote in a Monday post on Truth Social.

Trump had already called for Huang’s return on Friday, telling reporters after his trip to Asia that he wanted the former Nvidia chief to “make a big apology and go back.”

Trump’s remarks come after US Treasury Scott Bessent also seemingly softened his earlier calls for the company’s board to implement a “dramatic shake-up” of the company and to look outside for new leadership.

Asked Sunday if Trump’s recent support for Huang contradicted his own call, Bessent declined to say whether Huang should return.

“I think we have to see where the buck stops,” he said, referring to any potential non-compliance with US export controls.

Polymarket shows traders have placed a 37% chance that Huang will rejoin Nvidia by Dec. 31, 2027.

data.title: Asian Markets A Sea Of Red Amid Tech Selloff
data.description:
CANBERA (dpa-AFX) - Asian stock markets are a sea of red on Monday, following the broadly negative cues from Wall Street on Friday, dragged by a selloff in semiconductor and technology stocks, particularly in South Korea, mirroring their peers on tech-heavy Nasdaq amid concerns over tighter AI regulations and controls over chip export. The intermittent escalation in the geopolitical tensions in the Middle East also weighed on market sentiment. Asian markets closed mostly lower on Friday.

Iran has launched attacks on Bahrain over the weekend as they continue to targeting US assets in neighboring countries in the Middle East. However, US President Donald Trump has refrained from launching further strikes on Iran, but indicated he may consider resuming military action after the New Year if no peace agreement is reached.

The Australian stock market is modestly lower on Monday, extending the losses in the previous seven sessions, following the broadly positive cues from Wall Street on Friday. The benchmark S&P/ASX 200 index is falling well below the 8,600.00 level, with weakness in financial and technology stocks nearly offset by gains in mining and energy stocks.

The benchmark S&P/ASX 200 Index is losing 20.00 points or 0.23 percent to 8,572.60, after hitting a low of 8,528.50 earlier. The broader All Ordinaries Index is down 19.80 points or 0.23 percent to 8,673.00. Australian stocks closed sharply lower on Friday.

Among the major miners, BHP Group is gaining almost 2 percent and Mineral Resources is advancing almost 1 percent, while Rio Tinto and Fortescue are edging up 0.2 to 0.5 percent each.

Oil stocks are mostly higher. Origin Energy and Beach energy are edging up 0.3 percent each, while Woodside Energy is losing more than 1 percent. Santos is flat.

Among tech stocks, Afterpay owner Block is losing almost 2 percent, WiseTech Global is edging down 0.2 percent and Xero is declining more than 1 percent, while Appen is gaining almost 2 percent. Zip is tumbling more than 9 percent.

Gold miners are mostly higher. Resolute Mining is up more than 1 percent, Newmont is advancing almost 1 percent and Northern Star Resources is edging up 0.4 percent, while Evolution Mining and Genesis Minerals are gaining more than 2 percent each.

Among the big four banks, Commonwealth Bank and ANZ Banking are declining more than 1 percent each, while Westpac is down almost 1 percent and National Australia Bank is edging down 0.3 percent.

In other news, shares in EchoIQ are surging almost 11 percent after CEO Dustin Haines resigned ahead of its AGM scheduled for tomorrow. CFO Andrew Grover was named interin CEO.

In economic news, the manufacturing sector in Australia continued to contract in November, and at a faster pace, the latest survey from S&P Global revealed on Monday with a manufacturing PMI score of 48.7. That's down from 49.6 in October and it moves further beneath the boom-or-bust line of 50 that separates expansion from contraction.

The survey also showed that the services PMI fell to 46.2 in November from 48.5 and the composite PMI slipped to 46.1 from 48.2 a month earlier.

In the currency market, the Aussie dollar is trading at $0.664 on Monday.

The Japanese stock market is closed for Labor Thanksgiving Day on Monday. Japanese shares ended sharply lower on Friday.

In the currency market, the U.S. dollar is trading in the higher 158 yen-range on Monday.

Elsewhere in Asia, South Korea is tumbling 5.0 percent, while New Zealand, China, Hong Kong and Singapore are lower by between 1.4 and 1.8 percent each. Malaysia and Indonesia are down 0.5 and 0.3 percent, respectively. Taiwan is relatively flat.

On Wall Street, stocks showed an even more substantial move to the downside during trading on Friday following the steep losses seen during Thursday's session. The major averages went into a tailspin as the day progressed, closing sharply lower.

The Nasdaq plummeted 1,261.47 points or 5.3 percent to 22,617.73, the S&P 500 also plunged 265.44 points or 3.7 percent to 6,910.39 and the Dow slumped 949.73 points or 1.9 percent to 48,147.33.

The major European markets also showed significant moves to the downside. While the German DAX Index plunged 2.6 percent, the French CAC 40 Index slumped by 1.9 percent and the U.K.'s FTSE 100 Index slid by 1 percent.

Crude oil prices moved higher on Friday as vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz continue to suffer attacks. West Texas Intermediate crude for December delivery was up by $0.72 or 0.87 percent at $83.93 per barrel.

data.title: China's government-backed funds ramp up ETF buying to record as rout deepens
data.description:
China’s government-backed funds invested a record sum in the market on Friday, making another determined effort to halt an intensifying selloff.

Inflows into nine exchange-traded funds actively traded by the so-called national team reached 90 billion yuan ($13.5 billion) on Friday.

As per a Bloomberg report, this investment figure exceeded the previous record of 87 billion yuan, set during the April 2025 market rout triggered by US tariffs. The Harvest CSI 300 ETF received a record 23 billion yuan, while the ChinaAMC SSE 50 ETF attracted an all-time high of 21.7 billion yuan.

The intervention is part of a series of measures Beijing has taken to revive confidence after a months-long selloff drove the benchmark CSI 300 Index into a bear market. On Sunday, authorities relaxed margin-financing rules, reducing the minimum requirement for investors purchasing securities with borrowed funds from 100% to 80%.

The report further added that since October, China’s national team has increased purchases of the market’s largest ETFs as a selloff led by artificial intelligence stocks has worsened, but the buying has yet to establish a market floor. The benchmark index has fallen in every week since August except two.

Investors are also reducing their use of margin borrowing to buy stocks. The outstanding balance of margin trades fell 1.9% on Friday, its steepest decline since July 20.

The Chinese authorities have also lowered the cost of loans for corporate share buybacks and supplied liquidity to financial institutions to support additional stock purchases.

data.title: Viridis Mining and Minerals Receives Renewed European Union Backing for Colossus Project
data.description:
Viridis Mining and Minerals has moved its Colossus rare earth project closer to potential European institutional support after fresh talks in Brussels centred on investment and long-term commercial arrangements.

The discussions with senior European Commission officials follow a June visit to the Brazilian project by European commissioner Jozef Síkela, who has now publicly reaffirmed the European Union’s commitment to its development.

For Viridis, the diplomatic engagement comes as it assembles the financing required to build Colossus in Minas Gerais, where first production remains targeted for 2028.

Yet no new European funding agreement has been announced, with the latest discussions focused on identifying practical mechanisms rather than committing capital.

EU Reiterates Support

At the 20 November meeting, managing director Rafael Moreno held talks with Koen Doens, director-general for international partnerships, alongside Lucie Sestakova, head of cabinet to commissioner Síkela, and sustainable finance director Taneli Lahti.

The group examined ways European institutions might assist with investment, improve the project’s commercial competitiveness, and strengthen the supply chain that Viridis is developing between Brazil and Europe.

Commissioner Síkela subsequently reiterated his support, declaring that the EU was committed to progressing the project through development and eventual operations.

“Commissioner Síkela's public reaffirmation of the EU's commitment to Colossus further highlights the project's strategic relevance to Europe's critical raw materials objectives,” managing director Rafael Moreno said.

“Importantly, our discussions are progressing beyond strategic alignment towards potential financial support mechanisms that could further strengthen the project's financing structure and long-term commercial position.”

Long-Term Solvay Agreement

The commercial link to Europe is already taking shape through a binding long-term take-or-pay offtake agreement with Solvay, under which rare earth material from Colossus would feed the group’s separation operations in La Rochelle, France.

That agreement gives the proposed Brazilian operation a committed European customer while positioning its output within the EU’s efforts to diversify rare earth supply chains.

Colossus is expected to supply a range of rare earth elements including neodymium, praseodymium, dysprosium, and terbium, alongside samarium, yttrium, and gadolinium.

European representatives visited Viridis’ demonstration plant at its Rare Earth Research and Processing Centre in Poços de Caldas during June, discussing supply-chain cooperation and opportunities to transfer separation technology to Brazil.

Financing And Permits

Having completed a definitive feasibility study in August, Viridis has secured strategic equity commitments that it considers sufficient to cover its indicative equity requirement for Colossus.

Attention is now on senior debt, with international lenders, export credit agencies, and development finance institutions involved in discussions that have yet to produce final financing arrangements.

Engineering and procurement are moving ahead of a final investment decision, including mobilisation of a preferred engineering, procurement and construction management contractor and orders for major long-lead equipment.

The project already holds a preliminary licence in Brazil, but its application for an installation licence remains under assessment by environmental authorities.

Together, the funding, regulatory, and execution workstreams will determine whether Viridis can translate European political support and its supply agreement into the planned 2028 production start.

data.title: India's APL Apollo to buy two Tata Steel units
data.description:
APL Apollo Tubes (BSE: 533758) will buy Tata Steel (BSE: 500470)'s coated steel subsidiary and its tubes business for a combined INR280bn ($3.02bn) in cash, the Indian steel pipe maker said in a stock exchange filing on November 22.

The board approved both deals at a one-hour meeting convened at short notice. The bigger of the two transactions is the purchase of all shares in Tata Steel Colors Private Limited for INR163bn. APL Apollo also agreed to take over Tata Steel's tubes undertaking as a going concern through a slump sale for INR117bn.

The company said it wants to combine similar operations into a single, stronger business, with the added capacity giving it a wider distribution network and greater scale. Tata Steel Colors, previously known as Tata BlueScope Steel Private Limited, makes and sells colour-coated steel products and building solutions. It is based in Pune and operates only in India. The company booked turnover of roughly INR46.8bn in the financial year ended March 31, 2026, compared with about INR42.34bn in each of the two preceding years. Its net worth stood at roughly INR10.16bn and its profit after tax at about INR850mn.

APL Apollo will buy the 866mn shares of Tata Steel Colors from Tata Steel Limited and Tata Steel Downstream Products Limited under a share purchase agreement. The unit will become a wholly owned subsidiary once the deal closes. Both transactions need clearance from the Competition Commission of India and approval from APL Apollo shareholders. Shareholders must pass a special resolution under Section 186(3) of the Companies Act, 2013 for the share purchase.

The company said it will issue a separate notice for the shareholder vote. Under the business transfer agreement, APL Apollo will pay the full price for the tubes undertaking in cash when the deal completes. The sale covers the unit's assets, contracts, licences, employees and assumed liabilities, without separate values for individual items. It will go ahead only after the Tata Steel Colors acquisition has closed. APL Apollo said neither deal counts as a related party transaction. Both agreements set March 31, 2028 as the long stop date.

data.title: After Blockbuster Anthropic IPO, OpenAI Wants AI Rivals To Agree On Development ‘Limits’, While Meta Calls For Controlled Approach
data.description:
Key points:
  • Meta’s Alexandr Wang cautioned that technological progress could outpace humanity's ability to understand or control its consequences.
  • Last week, California sued OpenAI, alleging that it misled and endangered the public by knowingly developing AI models without necessary safeguards. 
  • Retail sentiment for ANT remained ‘extremely bullish,’ unchanged since its IPO.

OpenAI’s chief scientist has proposed that AI companies agree to limits on developing powerful models until they can better understand and monitor their behavior.

In a new blog post, Jakub Pachocki said developers should use ‘perplexity’ as a common measure of model capability amid growing concern about AI risks. Perplexity measures how well a model predicts the next token on average, with lower scores indicating better predictions, Pachocki said

“I further propose common limits, based on perplexity and other measurements, that developers are committed to not crossing until our ability to understand and monitor AI behavior achieves a certain concrete milestone,” he wrote.

AI could drive advances in AI training methods as early as 2027, Pachocki said, calling on developers not to cross agreed capability thresholds, based on perplexity and other measurements

Resharing the blog on X, CEO Sam Altman wrote: “We are providing a lot of transparency into our pretraining progress and hope we can agree as a field to common limits. I think that would be very wise and help ensure safety and control.”

The proposal comes a week after California sued the AI lab, alleging that it misled and endangered the public by knowingly developing AI models without necessary safeguards. The state’s attorney general’s suit cited the July Hugging Face attack, among other claims, as the basis.

Meanwhile, investors are closely watching rival Anthropic, which just wrapped up its blockbuster IPO. ANT stock rose 17% in Thursday’s trading but lost steam after that. The stock rose marginally in overnight trading late Thursday amid a relief rally in the broader tech market.

Meta Joins AI Safety Call

Meta Platforms’ Alexandr Wang warned that the arrival of superintelligence could fundamentally reshape humanity, arguing that models have largely overcome the intelligence barrier and calling for safety measures, according to a blog post on X.

He said AI models will eventually automate research into their own development, becoming "clearly superhuman at improving themselves," while accelerating advances in biology, cybersecurity and weapons research.

Wang cautioned that technological progress could outpace humanity's ability to understand or control its consequences. "It is hard to imagine a world where humanity can maintain control over fully unconstrained recursive self-improvement," he wrote, calling for urgent progress in safety, alignment and security.

Retail View For AI Firms 

On Stocktwits, the retail sentiment for ANT remained ‘extremely bullish,’ unchanged since its IPO. The sentiment was ‘bullish’ for OpenAI and ‘bearish’ for META.

“$ANT the Riemann hypothesis cracking machine isn’t going anywhere. Their proprietary tech and know-how is what’s valuable, not hardware. Given that they’re hardware constrained and are still busting centuries old proofs is actually more bullish, their models do most of the lifting,” said a trader.

data.title: South Korea vows to stabilise stock market after KOSPI drops 5%
data.description:
By Yena Park and Cynthia Kim

South Korea reiterated plans on Monday to stabilise its stock market if needed, as the KOSPI plummeted 5% and Finance Minister Lee Hyoung-il projected solid economic growth next year.

The benchmark index extended declines as concerns over the AI trade and a broader technology selloff overwhelmed the government's assurances that stabilisation funds would be deployed immediately if conditions worsened.

"Given the high impact of external uncertainties, volatility in our stock market has expanded significantly, which is why we addressed the issue. The message we delivered yesterday is that we will decide whether to activate measures depending on market conditions," Lee said at a press conference in Sejong.

"Accordingly, we are preparing so that necessary steps tailored to the situation will be implemented at an appropriate time."

On Sunday, the authorities said they would deploy market stabilisation funds immediately if conditions deteriorated, after the South Korean benchmark index tumbled to a 10-month low last week.

Lee said Asia's fourth-largest economy was maintaining strong momentum and could achieve growth in the upper-3% range if present trends continued.

Despite the upbeat baseline outlook, Lee warned that external risks remained severe, citing regulatory uncertainty surrounding the artificial intelligence industry, geopolitical instability and rising global interest rates. He cautioned that volatility in the semiconductor sector could spill over and amplify broader macroeconomic swings.

Asked whether South Korea could revise rules related to short-selling, Lee said the government's plan was to place greater emphasis on cracking down on illegal short-selling and strengthening surveillance against unfair trading rather than pursuing additional deregulation.

South Korea imposed a blanket short-selling ban in late 2023 to curb market volatility and illegal trading, lifting the 17-month prohibition in March 2025 after launching a centralised detection system.

data.title: PolyNovo Submits US FDA Pre-Market Approval for NovoSorb BTM Full-Thickness Burns Treatment
data.description:
Medical technology company PolyNovo has submitted a pre-market approval (PMA) application to the US Food and Drug Administration for NovoSorb biodegradable temporising matrix (BTM) to manage full-thickness burns.

The submission included a final report from the company’s pivotal US trial of 120 patients that demonstrated the product could achieve adjusted mean wound closure of 94.9% four weeks after skin grafting compared with 87.3% for standard of care (SOC) treatments.

For the primary composite safety endpoint, NovoSorb BTM recorded an event rate of 18.1% compared with 21.6% for SOC, with the results supporting the product’s safety profile and showing no evidence of increased risk.

If granted, PolyNovo’s submission—which was completed ahead of its previously stated year-end target—would allow the company to actively market NovoSorb BTM in the US and pursue expanded reimbursement and market access opportunities internationally.

Pivotal Randomised Trial

PolyNovo’s complex randomised controlled trial evaluated the safety and effectiveness of NovoSorb BTM to SOC treatments including a dermal matrix containing cross-linked bovine collagen and chondroitin 6-sulfate or cadaveric allograft.

Funded by the Biomedical Advanced Research and Development Authority, it recruited 120 patients between 18 years and 75 years of age across 24 US burn centres and three sites in India who had sustained 3% to 60% total body surface area deep dermal or full-thickness thermal burns.

Mr Peatey said the trial was one of the “largest controlled evaluations in the burns space undertaken to date”, and “the culmination of many years of clinical research”.

NovoSorb BTM has already achieved significant adoption in the US without an on-label indication for full-thickness burns, achieving commercial sales of $89.9 million in financial year 2026.

Pre-market approval would allow PolyNovo to support broader adoption in US burns with Level 1 randomised clinical evidence and actively market Novosorb BTM for full-thickness burns.

Product Launch Activities

Chief executive officer Bruce Peatey said the company was finalising product launch activities including market access, pricing and commercial readiness ahead of the expected PMA approval.

“NovoSorb BTM has built a strong position in the US and this submission is an important step forward so we are already preparing for the opportunities that approval could bring,” he said.

“We are increasing our investment in clinical evidence generation, marketing and reimbursement expertise to support further adoption of the product and expand its use across more indications.”

“The US trial represented a major milestone for PolyNovo and our team is excited about the potential to help more patients with complex injuries regain function and get back to their lives.”

data.title: Biotech Funds Slide Into Thanksgiving Week — Capricor’s FDA Fight And Back-To-Back Drug Decisions Top Watchlist
data.description:
Key points:
  • Kymera reports results for its eczema pill on Monday, while Invivyd shares interim data on its antibody for COVID-19 prevention.
  • BioLineRx and Agilent report quarterly results on Monday, followed by Medtronic on Tuesday.
  • DiaMedica will share early data on Tuesday from 12 participants in its study of DM199 for fetal growth restriction.

After a selloff that sent biotech funds down over 6%, investors are heading into Thanksgiving week with Capricor contesting an FDA rejection, two drugmakers reporting results on Monday and two more awaiting regulatory decisions after the holiday.

Biotech still fared better than the broader market last week. The iShares Biotechnology ETF (IBB) fell 6.1%, the Health Care Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLV) lost 6.2%, and the SPDR S&P Biotech ETF (XBI) dropped 6.9%. The SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (SPY) slid 8.6%, while the Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ) sank 10.5%.

DateCompany or eventWhat to watch
Nov.23Capricor (CAPR)Discusses the FDA’s rejection of Deramiocel for DMD
Nov.23Kymera (KYMR)Reports Phase 2b results for KT-621, its once-daily eczema pill.
Nov.23Invivyd (IVVD)Reports interim Phase 3 results for Ibramvibart, its antibody for COVID-19 prevention.
Nov.23BioLineRx (BLRX) and Agilent (A)BioLineRx reports Q3 results and Agilent reports Q4 results.
Nov.24DiaMedica (DMAC)Presents early Phase 2 findings on DM199 in fetal growth restriction.
Nov.24Medtronic (MDT)Reports Q2 results.
Nov.27BridgeBio (BBIO)FDA target date for BBP-418 in limb-girdle muscular dystrophy type 2I/R9.
Nov.28PolyPid (PYPD)FDA target date for D-Plex 100 to prevent surgical-site infections after colorectal surgery.

Capricor Defends DMD Data After FDA Rejection

Capricor Therapeutics will face investors on Monday with a question at the heart of the FDA’s rejection: How strong is the evidence that Deramiocel helps people with Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) retain the use of their arms?

The FDA said on Friday that Hope-3, the main trial of Capricor’s cell therapy, missed its original goals. The agency also cited unauthorized changes to the plan for analyzing the results and violations of rules designed to keep treatment assignments secret. The agency said that these problems made the results unreliable.

However, Capricor maintains that Hope-3 and an earlier trial both met their main goals. “We stand behind the rigor of our clinical program and the integrity of our data, and we believe the data support approval,” CEO Linda Marban said on Friday. The company said it would outline its next steps after reviewing the FDA’s letter.

Kymera And Invivyd Report Eczema And COVID Trial Results

Kymera Therapeutics’ once-daily pill, KT-621, showed promise in an early study of 22 people with moderate to severe eczema. After four weeks, eczema severity scores had fallen by an average of 63%. Everyone in the study took the pill. Monday’s Phase 2b results will show how three doses compare with a placebo over 16 weeks.

Invivyd’s Monday update could shape its bid for accelerated FDA approval of Ibramvibart, an antibody designed to prevent symptomatic COVID-19. The interim Phase 3 results will cover safety and how well antibodies in participants’ blood neutralize the virus. Whether fewer people who received ibramvibart developed symptoms is a question for later. The trial is continuing, and the case counts for each group remain under wraps.

Earnings Reports And DiaMedica’s Pregnancy Trial

BioLineRx will report third-quarter (Q3) results on Monday, a week after it said a fourth group of patients had begun taking GLIX1, its experimental treatment for an aggressive brain cancer called high-grade glioma. Additionally, lab equipment maker Agilent Technologies will also report on Monday, with fourth-quarter (Q4) sales guidance of $1.98 billion to $2 billion. Medical device maker Medtronic reports its second-quarter (Q2) results on Tuesday.

On the other hand, DiaMedica Therapeutics will share early results on Tuesday from a Phase 2 study of DM199 in pregnancies where the fetus grows more slowly than expected. In severe cases, doctors may need to deliver the baby before 32 weeks. The update will cover the first 12 participants, each of whom received one of two doses, and will offer an early look at the drug’s safety.

BridgeBio And PolyPid Await FDA Decisions After Thanksgiving

BridgeBio Pharma could secure the first U.S. treatment for a rare form of muscular dystrophy the day after Thanksgiving. The FDA’s target date is Friday or BBP-418, an oral drug for limb-girdle muscular dystrophy type 2I/R9. The disease gradually weakens the muscles people rely on to walk and breathe.

In BridgeBio’s Phase 3 trial, a difference in walking ability emerged as early as three months. After a year, patients taking BBP-418 completed a 100-meter test about 31 seconds faster than those taking placebo. “In a progressive muscle disease where time matters, seeing early improvements in ambulation suggests a rapid onset of action of BBP-418,” said Katherine Mathews of the University of Iowa, who presented the findings in March.

Meanwhile, PolyPid’s FDA deadline follows on Saturday. Its treatment, D-Plex 100 releases the antibiotic doxycycline directly at the incision to help prevent infection after colorectal surgery. In a Phase 3 trial, 3.8% of patients who received it alongside standard care developed an infection at the incision, compared with 9.5% of those who received standard care alone. PolyPid and its U.S. partner, Azurity Pharmaceuticals, are preparing for an early 2027 launch if the FDA approves the treatment.

data.title: Top Auto Stock Picks: Ambit lists three names it is betting on, cites triggers for re-rating
data.description:
Auto stocks are in focus as brokerage firm Ambit Capital expects steady demand and comfortable margins to drive re-rating for the sector.

In its latest note on Monday, November 23, Ambit Capital said that original equipment makers (OEMs) have healthy order books and low channel inventory. The average selling price growth in the second quarter was better than expected across most OEMs, it said.

The spot commodity basket is down between 6% - 8% compared to the second quarter levels for passenger vehicles and two-wheelers. Lower commodities, price hikes and operating leverage will drive margin recovery, it added.

Ambit Capital said the earnings downgrade cycle is largely behind the passenger vehicle OEMs.

The brokerage has raised its volume estimates by 1%-3% across segments. It also raised its earnings per share (EPS) estimates by 2%-5% for two-wheeler OEMs, and by 6%-10% for passenger vehicle OEMs.

Ambit Capital's top "buys" are Hyundai Motor India, Eicher Motors and Mahindra and Mahindra (M&M).

data.title: Indian rupee could rise to 91.50/$ on equity inflows, HDFC Bank's treasury head says
data.description:
By Ira Dugal

The Indian rupee could gain to 91.50 against the US dollar if equity inflows remain strong and geopolitical risks stay in check, a top treasury official at the country's largest private bank said.

The Indian currency depreciated sharply till October, declining 8% against the US dollar at the lowest point of the year as foreign investors withdrew from equity markets in Asia's third-largest economy due to high valuations and lack of AI investments.

Higher oil prices added to the pressure, prompting tough measures from the central bank, including a reserve requirement against large hedging transactions.

Markets turned in November, with global investors pumping a monthly record $12 billion into Indian equities.

"I believe 91.50 could be a possibility," said Arup Rakshit, group head for treasury at HDFC Bank in Mumbai in an interview late on Friday, adding that he sees the currency trading in a range of 91.50 to 93.50 in the near term.

On Friday, the rupee closed at 92.67 to the dollar.

The rupee has gained nearly 2.5% in November, turning sentiment in the offshore non-deliverable forwards market and prompting exporters to sell dollars, Rakshit said.

Additional dollar demand brought on by the Reserve Bank of India's decision to impose a 20% foreign exchange risk reserve on large hedging transactions has also eased, he added.

"When the Reserve Bank of India introduced a foreign exchange risk reserve there was some additional dollar demand that came in from importers as absolute hedged import rates were lower, since the INR had immediately appreciated," Rakshit said.

"That demand is now reducing as the import cycle is typically 90 days and nearly half of that is over," he said, adding that importers are hedging less as the rupee strengthens and oil prices fall.

A 50 BASIS POINT HIKE?

While pressure on the currency has eased, inflation has breached the central bank's upper tolerance limit of 6%, prompting a few analysts to expect a 50 basis point hike at its December meeting.

Rakshit does not rule this out.

"I think the repo rate will settle somewhere between 6.25-6.5%. A 25 basis point hike in December is more or less given. There is a section of the market which is thinking it could be a 50 basis point hike and I would lean on that side," he said.

Retail inflation rose to 6.09% in October and wholesale inflation rose to 12.3%.

Higher wholesale prices have yet to fully pass through into retail prices, Rakshit said, adding that food prices are also starting to rise.

This will prompt the central bank to raise rates and keep liquidity tight at 0.6% to 1% of banking system deposits, he said.

Bond yields would also rise, but not sharply, he said.

"Immediately, I would put the top for the 10-year at about 7.40% and then moving up to 7.50% to 7.60 levels max. I don't see it going beyond that," he said.

data.title: SNDK Stock Wrapped Its Worst Week Since July: Why Morningstar Sees A NAND Memory Bust Looming For SanDisk
data.description:
Key points:
  • Morningstar says SanDisk lacks pricing power and a lasting advantage in the crowded NAND market. 
  • High manufacturing and research costs, combined with volatile chip prices, could limit SanDisk’s profit. 
  • Analyst Kerwin sees rising supply, Chinese competition, and weaker pricing could hurt performance from 2028 onward. 

SanDisk Corp. (SNDK) stock posted its worst weekly performance since July as investors weighed the sustainability of the AI-driven memory boom. Morningstar analyst William Kerwin warned that rising NAND production could trigger a supply glut, potentially pushing prices lower after a 2028 peak and squeezing SanDisk's profit.

SanDisk stock traded over 5% higher overnight Sunday, after a 28% plunge during the trading week.

AI Boom Could Mask SanDisk's Long-Term Weaknesses

Morningstar believes SanDisk operates in a highly competitive memory market where manufacturers have limited ability to influence selling prices. Differences in chip specifications offer little protection, allowing suppliers to quickly match tech advances. Consequently, strong earnings during periods of limited supply can disappear when manufacturers produce more chips than customers need.

The firm does not assign SanDisk an economic moat, arguing that expensive manufacturing requirements and unpredictable industry pricing make consistent long-term returns difficult. It estimates that capital spending consumes approximately 10% of SNDK’s revenue, while research and development expenses account for another 10%.

NAND Pricing Could Peak In 2028

Kerwin expects the memory industry's current expansion to continue over the next year, supported by demand from AI infrastructure, computers, smartphones and cloud services. It estimates NAND price increases in fiscal 2027 to lift SanDisk's revenue by nearly 150%.

The outlook begins to become weak afterward. New factories and production improvements could push industry supply growth beyond 30% annually between 2027 and 2029. Morningstar expects NAND pricing to reach its high point in fiscal 2028 before entering a decline that could extend through 2031.

Research from TrendForce also supports this theory and expects the NAND market to weaken in 2027, with prices falling as production increases.

The analyst also highlights competition from China's Yangtze Memory Technologies (YMTC), whose growing presence could add supply and intensify pricing pressure. Sandisk's relatively limited position in higher-margin enterprise storage products presents another competitive disadvantage.

SanDisk’s $110 Fair Value Estimate Signals Caution

After SanDisk's eight-for-one stock split last week, Morningstar set its fair value at $110 per share. The analyst expects profits and operating margins to decline as memory chip prices fall.

The firm's Very High uncertainty assessment also reflects the possibility of another severe industry contraction. During the 2023 downturn, SanDisk's revenue fell 37%, and gross margin dropped to 7%.

SNDK Stock: Retail View 

However, on Stocktwits, retail sentiment around the stock remained ‘bullish’ with a 142% increase in message volume over the past week.

A user said, “Pullback of a lifetime. Oversold. Undervalued. Fair value 3X from here.”

Another user said, “I remember when googl# was 90 and I bought that. I’m thinking this is a good entry here.”

SNDK stock has gained 167% year-to-date.
